races.name: FBC Manby Bowdler Mares' Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: She Is For Me Boys
runners_data.note: Front-running style suits small field dynamics, returns to form evident at Fakenham, tongue-tie applied suggests renewed focus
runners_data.comment: Close third in valuable mares' chase at Market Rasen last month; ought to be hard to beat
runners_data.spotlight: 1-6 over fences; returned to form of late and although a beaten favourite when runner-up at Fakenham (2m5f, good) last month, that was still a creditable effort; tongue-tie now added; the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Charity Barnum
runners_data.note: Hold-up style faces 13-race losing streak, Irish raider with limited chase experience but decent hurdles form foundation
runners_data.comment: Best hurdles run when second at this venue last August, no impact in two races over fences
runners_data.spotlight: Irish raider; 13-race maiden whose best effort came over hurdles when a close second at Tramore (2m5f, good) last August, but three attempts over fences have seen her pulled up twice and tailed off once; Sean Bowen booked and, while a return to better ground and handicap company may help, she still has plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Laffer Curve
runners_data.note: Prominent runner benefits from strong Skelton stable form, finished weakly at Huntingdon suggests stamina queries remain
runners_data.comment: Need to find a bit with Onefournine on the figures but should be thereabouts.
runners_data.spotlight: Showed promise in maiden/novice hurdles before running respectably when third on handicap debut at Huntingdon (2m4f, good) in March; finished weakly over a slightly longer trip at Newton Abbot (2m5f, good) the following month but has since undergone wind surgery; now switches to fences from what looks a workable mark (eased 2lb) and commands respect.

runners_data.name: Miss Denver
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare carries significant weight advantage at 143lbs, recent Newton Abbot third shows current form but chase debut unknown
runners_data.comment: Kept on for third on recent handicap hurdle debut; could have more to offer over fences
runners_data.spotlight: Well-bred mare; kept on for a respectable third on handicap hurdle debut at Newton Abbot (2m1f, good) last month and shaped reasonably well on chase debut at Stratford (2m1f, good to firm) where she jumped soundly; pedigree suggests this longer trip should suit and a first-time hood may also eke out a little more, now eased 2lb.

races.paceDynamic: She Is For Me Boys will take this race forward from the outset, setting a sustainable tempo without pressure from fellow prominent runner Laffer Curve who tends to track rather than lead. The hold-up horses Charity Barnum and Miss Denver will settle at the back in this small field, looking to pick up the pieces late. With only four runners and a confirmed front-runner facing minimal early pressure, the pace will be modest early before quickening significantly from the final circuit. This sustainable gallop clearly favors the front-running and prominent horses who can control their own destiny rather than relying on a strong pace to bring hold-up horses into contention.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If She Is For Me Boys jumps cleanly and maintains her rhythm...
scenarios.body: The pace will be perfectly controlled throughout, allowing her superior class (OR 109) to tell as others struggle to close the gap. Gavin Sheehan can dictate terms from the front and kick clear when ready.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Laffer Curve travels strongly behind the leader and pounces late...
scenarios.body: The Dan Skelton-trained mare can use her tactical speed to overcome the modest pace and strike in the final furlong. Harry Skelton's timing will be crucial to capitalize on any weakening of the front-runner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Success
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens significantly from three out onwards...
scenarios.body: Miss Denver's recent good form over shorter can translate to this trip if given a truly-run race to aim at. The 20lb weight advantage becomes telling in a strongly-run finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Maiden Breakthrough
scenarios.trigger: If Charity Barnum finds significant improvement over fences...
scenarios.body: The Irish raider's hurdles form suggests ability, and Sean Bowen might have found the key to unlocking her chasing potential. A breakthrough performance could catch the others off-guard.

watchPoints.text: She Is For Me Boys must handle the responsibility of making the running alone - any jumping errors could prove fatal
Laffer Curve showed stamina concerns last time and needs to prove this trip suits her prominent style
Charity Barnum's fence jumping remains questionable given three unsuccessful chase attempts to date
Miss Denver steps up significantly in trip from her recent hurdles success over two miles one furlong
The modest pace scenario strongly disadvantages both hold-up horses who need a strong gallop to be competitive

races.name: CopyBet Supporting UK Horse Racing Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Axel Bleue
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid form on good ground but pulled up on handicap debut suggests question marks over this discipline
runners_data.comment: Could appreciate returning to a handicap but current wellbeing is a bit of an issue
runners_data.spotlight: Point and dual bumper winner in 2025; runner-up in two 2m7f novice hurdles in October but pulled up on handicap debut the following month and has offered little in two runs this spring since a break, including when beaten 24l on last month's chase debut; probably on a workable mark but needs the cheekpieces to have a positive effect.

runners_data.name: Redbridge Rambler
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits the likely pace scenario and recent Warwick win over 3m on good ground shows he's in form
runners_data.comment: Won at Warwick yesterday; he would have to be respected if running again today
runners_data.spotlight: Showed the benefit of April's reappearance when back up to a more suitable stamina test off a reduced mark and winning at Warwick (3m, good) the following month; back up 3lb but Freddie Keighley can claim his full allowance; a big player if repeating the effort.

runners_data.name: The Flying Poet
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who needs strong pace to be effective but recent Perth win gives confidence over fences
runners_data.comment: Off the mark in tight finish here (3m, good; 13-8 fav) last September; switches to fences.
runners_data.spotlight: Broke his duck over hurdles after a few near misses and made a winning start to fences at Perth (3m) on his return from a break last month, albeit narrowly with the second making a costly error at the last; lacked fluency there but kept on well and, although a 6lb higher mark asks a question, another bold bid can be expected.

runners_data.name: Hall Lane
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with three recent seconds suggesting his turn is imminent, particularly effective on good ground
runners_data.comment: Only 1-13 over fences but is threatening to double his tally; possibilities
runners_data.spotlight: 1-13 over fences but has been shaping as though his turn is near again after finishing runner-up on his last three starts, all around this trip on good ground when ridden by Jack Hogan; likely to be in the mix again off an unchanged mark.

runners_data.name: Jongleur d'Etoiles
runners_data.note: Hold-up style requires genuine pace but 85 days since last run raises fitness concerns despite ability
runners_data.comment: Hurdles winner at up to 3m2f; close to breaking chase duck latest; big player.
runners_data.spotlight: Multiple hurdles winner at up to 3m2f, including on a sound surface; 0-6 over fences but went very close at Doncaster (3m2f, good to soft) in March having looked the likely winner; leading contender from an unchanged mark, if repeating that effort.

runners_data.name: Atlanta Brave
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but hasn't won for three years and inconsistent form makes him hard to trust
runners_data.comment: Has become disappointing but his third at Hereford was better (3m1f, good)
runners_data.spotlight: Hasn't won for three years and struggles for consistency; made an encouraging return when third at Hereford (3m1f, good) in March but couldn't back it up when well beaten at Bangor in refitted cheekpieces last time; blinkers now replace them but others appeal more.

runners_data.name: Gata Ban
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner carrying just 145lbs whose recent Fontwell second suggests fencing improvement but needs pace collapse
runners_data.comment: Ran big race in defeat over C&D 18 days ago and gets another chance off same mark today
runners_data.spotlight: 0-7 over fences but ran big race in defeat when second at Fontwell (3m2f, good) last month, looking the likely winner until collared on run-in; one of two for the stable and a player off same mark again today.

runners_data.name: Jullou De Grissay
runners_data.note: Prominent runner on same mark as last win but 51-day break and amateur jockey adds complication
runners_data.comment: Good-ground hurdle winner; dual point winner who should make a chaser
runners_data.spotlight: On the same mark as when winning over hurdles (2m7f, good) last summer, ridden by James King; shaped as though the run was needed in March on return from an absence, before finishing a well-beaten second of three on chase debut the following month; has since undergone wind surgery and retains potential over fences.

runners_data.name: Captain Boudet
runners_data.note: Likely leader with tactical advantage but 81 days off and inconsistent record raises reliability questions
runners_data.spotlight: Won over 2m3f at Exeter off 1lb lower in March 2025; inconsistent in five starts last season for Jeremy Scott, signing off with a fair second back at Exeter two and a half months ago; has changed hands since and goes back up in trip on stable debut with a visor added; on a good mark if able to put his best foot forward.

runners_data.name: Jack To Bat
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who has disappointed in two handicap chase starts since switching from hurdles
runners_data.spotlight: £130,000 buy after runner-up in an Irish point in 2023 and showed promise over hurdles, but his two efforts since switched to fences/handicaps this year have been disappointing; wore this headgear when a remote fourth of four at Wetherby (3m, good to soft) in March and has since undergone wind surgery.

runners_data.name: Est Illic
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with 12-year-old legs but weight allowance and recent hunter chase form provides outside hope
runners_data.comment: A modest performer under rules these days and his Ludlow third was remote
runners_data.spotlight: Point winner in April but his rules form is modest; although placed under Jess Stewart on both recent runs in hunter chases, he's been well held; needs to find plenty more back in handicap company.

runners_data.name: Stay Hopeful
runners_data.note: Prominent early but fades late, carrying bottom weight but poor form over hurdles questions ability
runners_data.comment: Again well beaten on handicap debut but was only 5-1; could be given another chance
runners_data.spotlight: Irish point winner who has yet to show any worthwhile form over hurdles (2m-2m4f) on varying ground, including since switched to handicaps on his last two starts and fitted with cheekpieces; not entirely dismissed on this switch to fences off a basement mark but he needs to step up.

races.paceDynamic: Captain Boudet will dictate proceedings from the front with no obvious challengers for the early lead, allowing him to set a comfortable tempo through the first circuit. The prominent runners Redbridge Rambler, Hall Lane, and Axel Bleue will track the leader in a compact group, while hold-up horses The Flying Poet, Jongleur d'Etoiles, and Gata Ban will need to be wound up from the back. With just one confirmed front-runner and no pace pressure, this creates a tactical race where Captain Boudet can control the gallop and kick for home when it suits. This race shape strongly favours the prominent runners who can track the steady pace and strike when the tempo lifts, rather than hold-up horses who may find insufficient pace collapse to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Captain Boudet sets steady fractions and the prominent trackers position perfectly behind him
scenarios.body: The lack of pace pressure allows Redbridge Rambler, Hall Lane and Axel Bleue to travel comfortably before unleashing finishing kicks. Captain Boudet's controlled tempo suits those just behind rather than creating the collapse needed for back-markers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Captain Boudet quickens the tempo approaching the final circuit and his rivals fail to respond immediately
scenarios.body: The leader's tactical advantage becomes decisive as he stretches the field when it matters most. Prominent runners get caught flat-footed by the sudden injection of pace while hold-up horses are too far back to bridge the gap.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Charge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves faster than anticipated and Captain Boudet begins to weaken turning for home
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop sets up perfectly for The Flying Poet and Jongleur d'Etoiles to unleash their finishing kicks. Gata Ban's recent second at Fontwell suggests he can also benefit from a truly-run race with pace collapse.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the tactical battle between the main contenders allows a lightly-weighted runner to slip through unnoticed
scenarios.body: Stay Hopeful or Est Illic could benefit from their weight allowances if the pace sets up perfectly. The focus on the main protagonists might create gaps for unconsidered runners with nothing to lose.

watchPoints.text: Captain Boudet must be watched closely for how aggressively he sets the early fractions as this will determine the entire race dynamic
The Flying Poet and Jongleur d'Etoiles need monitoring for how they travel through the mid-race as hold-up horses require the right pace scenario
Redbridge Rambler's position behind Captain Boudet will be crucial as he needs to avoid getting caught in traffic when making his move
Hall Lane's jumping under pressure given three recent seconds suggests he's due but needs to handle the step up in class
Watch for any market moves on Gata Ban given his recent improvement and significant weight allowance

races.name: Law Without The Horsing Around Handicap Chase (Arc Summer Chase Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Jiair Madrik
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with recent wind surgery success, likely to dominate early but may tire if pressed late over this stamina-testing trip.
runners_data.spotlight: Took advantage of a declining mark to open his account over fences at Uttoxeter (2m5f, good) three weeks ago, on his second start following wind surgery; there should be more to come with that win under his belt and he may well follow up.

runners_data.name: Culligran
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning after 327 days off, stable debut for new connections makes her hard to assess despite previous chase-winning ability.
runners_data.spotlight: Scored on her second chase start at Newton Abbot (2m5f, good) last June for John O'Shea; absent since last July and makes stable debut; best watched unless the market speaks in her favour.

runners_data.name: The Moonlight Man
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with poor completing record, pulled up five times in seven starts suggests stamina or jumping issues remain problematic.
runners_data.spotlight: Point winner but has been pulled up on five of his seven starts under rules; hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: La Quarite
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning after 270 days off following handicap rise, previous 36-length win shows ability but long absence creates uncertainty.
runners_data.spotlight: Got off the mark over fences when scoring by 36l at Newton Abbot (2m5f, good) last July; the handicapper whacked him up 14lb and after four successive defeats he remains 11lb above his winning mark; must defy a 270-day absence.

runners_data.name: Applicationofcash
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in excellent recent form for new trainer, previous struggles over today's distance suggest stamina limitations may resurface.
runners_data.comment: Won at Taunton and he had an excuse when stepped back up to 2m4f latest; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Responsible for both of his new trainer's wins, the latest at this track (2m, good) 15 days ago; didn't appear to see his race out when tried over today's distance at Wincanton in April but he is clearly in good order.

runners_data.name: Pooroldmackley
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning to fences after hurdle campaign, claimed rider takes valuable weight off but form has declined markedly.
runners_data.spotlight: Scored over fences in April 2025 on heavy, and has won twice over hurdles since but has lost his form in that sphere; now returns to fences; hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Majestic Moment
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse maintaining consistent form, recent Fontwell second suggests continuing improvement trajectory over fences remains intact.
runners_data.comment: Two wins last month, the latter over C&D; unseated last time; still has strong claims
runners_data.spotlight: 3-7 over fences and remains in form following his second at Fontwell (2m3f, good) 13 days ago; may not have finished progressing yet and entitled to be on the shortlist.

runners_data.name: Song Of Earth
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with poor recent record, 79-day absence and declining form makes him hard to recommend despite lightweight burden.
runners_data.comment: 11yo who struggled on both starts towards the end of last year, following an absence
runners_data.spotlight: Sole success over fences was when trained in Ireland in April 2022; plenty of water under the bridge since and was well below form on all three starts last term; easy to oppose.

runners_data.name: Holy Legend
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with recent emphatic win, 10lb rise in weights following Fontwell success will test his continuing progress over fences.
runners_data.spotlight: Opened his account over fences with an emphatic win at Fontwell (2m2f, good) last month; will find it tougher off 10lb higher but should be kept onside.

runners_data.name: Noble Recall
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 253 days off, previous chase form was promising but lengthy absence creates significant fitness concerns.
runners_data.spotlight: Improved to win off lowly hurdle mark at Southwell (2m4f, good) in May last year; made satisfactory chase debut when fourth over C&D (good) last September but has been off since; this looks a tough assignment on his return.

races.paceDynamic: Jiair Madrik will lead from the front as the sole confirmed pace-setter, likely to get an uncontested lead through the early stages with The Moonlight Man and La Quarite settling prominently behind. The pace should be steady rather than searching, allowing the large contingent of hold-up horses including Culligran, Applicationofcash, Majestic Moment, Holy Legend and Noble Recall to get into contention turning for home. This tactical setup strongly favours the prominent racers and patient hold-up performers who can capitalise on the lack of early pace pressure, while making life difficult for any horse needing to be handy early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Jiair Madrik gets an easy lead and maintains galloping room
scenarios.body: The front-runner controls the tempo completely and kicks clear approaching the last fence when the chasers are still organising their challenges. Prominent trackers like La Quarite get first run but cannot reel in the leader's advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Brigade Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too slow and collapses in the home straight
scenarios.body: The patient hold-up horses get perfect conditions to unleash their finishing kicks simultaneously, creating a cavalry charge finish where class and recent form tell. Fresh legs and superior turn of foot prove decisive over those who've been closer to the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Timing
scenarios.trigger: If Jiair Madrik sets steady fractions but tires approaching two out
scenarios.body: The horses settled in second and third positions get the ideal sit behind the pace-setter and strike at the optimal moment when the leader weakens. They benefit from the tow without having to do the donkey work themselves.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Jiair Madrik goes too slow early and multiple horses challenge simultaneously
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where positioning and traffic problems determine the outcome more than ability. The winner emerges from a bunched field where luck in running proves crucial.

watchPoints.text: Jiair Madrik could get such an easy lead that he becomes unstoppable, with no other natural pace-setters to apply early pressure.
Culligran's stable debut after almost a year off makes her market moves crucial indicators of readiness and expectation levels.
The Moonlight Man's poor completing record suggests he could cause interference or disrupt the rhythm of horses around him.
Applicationofcash's stamina limitations over this distance need monitoring, particularly if he's still travelling well approaching the home turn.
Multiple hold-up horses could create traffic problems in the home straight if the pace collapses and they all challenge simultaneously.

races.name: Manby Not Mandy Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Delusionofgrandeur
runners_data.spotlight: 5,700euros foal, 13,000euros 3yo; third foal; dam 2m hurdle winner, half-sister to useful 2m-2m4f hurdle/chase Golden Hoof; beaten in all six maiden Irish points but in good hands and likely to show improvement under rules.

runners_data.name: Emerald Tir
runners_data.spotlight: £16,000 3yo; sixth foal; dam unraced sister to high-class 2m-3m1f hurdle/chase winner Menorah, out of 2m4f-2m6f hurdle/chase winning half-sister to thorough staying jumper Jet Boys; may need the run on debut.

runners_data.name: Litaque
runners_data.spotlight: 10,000euros 3yo, £5,000 Doncaster May 25; eighth foal; half-brother to winners Grozni (bumper and useful 2m4f-4m hurdle/chase) and Donskoye (French 2m6f chase); dam unraced half-sister to smart 2m1f-3m hurdle/chase winner Val De Ferbet; landed maiden point with the minimum of fuss 15 days ago, and could be hard to beat on this rules debut.

runners_data.name: Giant's Way
runners_data.spotlight: 58,000euros foal, 140,000euros 3yo; eighth foal; closely related to high-class 2m hurdler Labaik, half-brother to winners Danza De La Barre (French 7f-9.5f; RPR 72) and Aiguille Rouge (2m2f hurdle); dam French 5.5f winner (100), out of German 7f Listed winner; yard in decent nick at present and he is one to be interested in; tongue-tie fitted for debut.

runners_data.name: Master Tim
runners_data.spotlight: Second foal; dam placed in bumpers, sister to point winners Beyondthestorm and Coningbeg, half-sister to 3m1f/3m2f chase winner Kimora, out of unraced sister to bumper winner Culmore Native, half-sister to bumper/2m-2m4f hurdle winner Finns Cross; beaten 17l in a point in April; makes rules debut for yard that has occasional bumper success.

runners_data.name: Storm Dudley
runners_data.spotlight: Second foal; dam 1m-1m4f maiden (RPR 65), closely related to useful 7f-1m4f winner Cay Dancer, half-sister to 1m2f Listed winner Dynamic, out of French 1m/1m1f winning half-sister to 1m Group 1 winner Balisada; others appeal more.

runners_data.name: Redbarn
runners_data.spotlight: 50,000euros foal, 30,000euros 3yo, £25,000 Doncaster May 26; fourth foal; dam unraced sister to high-class French staying chaser Rubi Ball; a beaten favourite in a couple of Irish points; she looks likely to show significant improvement in the hands of champion trainer on rules debut.

runners_data.name: Ultimately
runners_data.comment: Out of half-sister to three Flat/one hurdle winners; trainer not known for bumper winners.
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten 27l on debut over C&D (good; 80-1) 15 days ago and may do better when he tackles hurdles.

runners_data.name: C'Est Pour Moi
runners_data.comment: £14,000 3yo; third foal; dam runner-up 2m4f chase; stable 15% in bumpers last two seasons.
runners_data.spotlight: Tailed off on debut at Worcester (2m, good; 8-1) 15 days ago with hood fitted (absent today); likely capable of better but big improvement required.

races.name: #Bepartofit Novices' Hurdle (Arc Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Pioneer Pete
runners_data.note: Front runner with class edge but 36-day break and making all the running poses tactical risk against hold-up horses
runners_data.spotlight: Got off the mark over hurdles at the fifth attempt in a Wetherby maiden (2m, good) in March; surpassed that with a cracking second in a big-field handicap at Punchestown (2m, yielding) in May and should be up to defying a 7lb penalty in this company.

runners_data.name: Solo Eclipse
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who struggled on good ground previously and carries headgear suggesting temperament issues
runners_data.comment: Failed to build on debut bumper second when sixth at Huntingdon; goes hurdling now
runners_data.spotlight: Made a promising start when runner-up in a bumper at Huntingdon (2m, soft) in February but hasn't progressed on good ground in a similar contest or on hurdles debut at Uttoxeter three weeks ago; may need soft to see him in a better light.

runners_data.name: Little Lady Rock
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from long 316-day layoff making hurdles debut, yard change adds uncertainty
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up in three bumpers last summer when trained by Ryan Potter; has changed yards since and best watched on her hurdles debut.

runners_data.name: Fine Fellow
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who was beaten 26 lengths on debut but should improve significantly with that experience
runners_data.comment: Fair third on debut but didn't build on it when well held in course bumper in December
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten 26l on hurdles debut at Warwick (2m, good; 25-1) four weeks ago; should do better once he gets a handicap mark.

runners_data.name: Thatsnotmyname
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with concerning fade-in-finish pattern and modest form, easy to dismiss
runners_data.comment: Well backed and well beaten on debut at Ludlow; should benefit from that but bit to prove.
runners_data.spotlight: Has shown only modest form in a bumper and on hurdles debut over C&D 15 days ago; easy to dismiss.

runners_data.name: Molten Sea
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with Flat speed transferring well to hurdles, 56-day break could be ideal
runners_data.comment: Quite useful on the Flat and she won by 14l over hurdles at Kempton last time; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Won three on the Flat for William Haggas; sold for 20,000gns to join this yard last October and scored on her second hurdles start at Kempton (2m good) in March; another good run when runner-up at Chepstow (2m, good to soft) the following month and should run her race.

runners_data.name: Miss Kingston
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who bolted up on British debut, tactical advantage in slowly-run race
runners_data.comment: Sets the standard on last of four starts in Ireland; much respected on stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: 0-6 when trained in Ireland; sold for 22,000gns to join current yard in January, and bolted up on her British debut in a Chepstow maiden (2m, good) in April; needs to be taken seriously even with a 7lb penalty.

runners_data.name: Mayo
runners_data.note: Hold-up type on hurdles debut after modest bumper form, stable debut adds unknown factor
runners_data.comment: Showed ability on the first of his two starts but improvement necessary on stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Best effort in third of three bumpers when third of four at Hereford (2m, good to firm) last month on stable debut; hurdles debut and needs to show more.

races.paceDynamic: Pioneer Pete stands alone as the confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the start in this small field. With Little Lady Rock and Molten Sea the only prominent racers, there's minimal early pressure allowing Pioneer Pete to bowl along at a comfortable gallop. The lack of pace pressure means the tempo will be steady rather than searching, setting up a tactical finish where positioning and timing matter more than raw speed. This controlled pace scenario strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce late kicks, as the leaders will have plenty left in the tank turning for home.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Pioneer Pete gets an easy lead with minimal harassment from the prominent pair
scenarios.body: The steady gallop allows hold-up horses to close strongly in the final two furlongs when the pace inevitably quickens. Late-running types with tactical speed get first run on a tiring leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pioneer Pete Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Pioneer Pete's class advantage (OR 124) proves decisive despite tactical disadvantage
scenarios.body: His superior rating and recent Wetherby win give him enough quality to resist late challenges even after making the running. The 36-day break has him fresh enough to sustain his effort.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Take Over
scenarios.trigger: If Little Lady Rock or Molten Sea press Pioneer Pete early and establish better tactical positions
scenarios.body: One of the prominent racers gets first run on the leader while holding off the late closers who leave their challenge too late. Their forward positions prove crucial in a slowly-run race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Hold-Up Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and a rank outsider produces an unexpected late surge
scenarios.body: The combination of weak pace and small field creates chaos in the final furlong where any horse with a turn of foot can strike. Mayo's stable debut improvement or Fine Fellow's handicap potential could surface.

watchPoints.text: Pioneer Pete could get loose on the lead if Little Lady Rock and Molten Sea don't press early enough
Miss Kingston and Mayo both held-up runners who need the pace to develop properly to show their best
Molten Sea's 56-day break timing after her Kempton hurdles win could have her spot-on for this
Fine Fellow was beaten 26 lengths on debut but that experience could unlock significant improvement
Little Lady Rock's 316-day absence and yard change makes her hurdles debut difficult to assess

races.name: Best Scrap Metal Prices CRS Malvern Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Presenting Milan
runners_data.note: Non-runner so tactical impact irrelevant despite hold-up style suiting the likely strong pace
runners_data.spotlight: Won bumper in 2024 and got off the mark on his second outing over hurdles in a Fontwell maiden (2m3f, good; 8-11) in May last year; absent since and makes handicap debut; fascinating contender; market will be best guide.

runners_data.name: Theatre Tom
runners_data.note: Hold-up style ideal for strong pace but 520 days off and making handicap debut suggests this comes too soon
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten in three points and in four novice/maiden hurdles; returns from a lengthy absence and makes handicap debut; likely to need the run; trainer also runs Castle Ivers and Trust House.

runners_data.name: Oakley
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits but needs holding up according to spotlight and proven at similar conditions with recent form edge
runners_data.comment: Not always reliable but won easily by over 8l at Hereford last week; carries 7lb penalty
runners_data.spotlight: Both wins over hurdles have came at Hereford over 2m3f on good; ran up to his best when runner-up at Fontwell (2m3f, good) last month; he needs to be held up to get the best out of him; this is a step up in class and he needs to improve further.

runners_data.name: Speed Davis
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with recent wins who could benefit from strong early pace but carrying penalty from April success
runners_data.comment: Good winner at Bangor (2m7f) last month but recent 7lb rise demands further progress
runners_data.spotlight: Completed a double, five months apart, when successful at Bangor (2m7f, good) in April; this is tougher off 7lb higher but may have more to offer in search of a three-timer.

runners_data.name: Castle Ivers
runners_data.note: Front-runner who made all last time and step up to 2m4f should suit but faces two other confirmed pace-setters
runners_data.comment: Useful bumper & maiden hurdle winner; tailed off on recent comeback run (h'cap debut).
runners_data.spotlight: Bumper winner who made it two out of three over hurdles at Perth (2m, good to soft) when making all; looks sure to be suited by this step up in trip and holds good claims.

runners_data.name: Continuance
runners_data.note: Another front-runner but may have needed last run after 10-month break and faces pace pressure from stablemates
runners_data.comment: Consistent and every chance provided he's straight enough after a lengthy break
runners_data.spotlight: Has three wins over hurdles at around 2m; may have needed the run on his first start since January when fourth of eight at Warwick (2m, good) last month and this step up in trip should suit.

runners_data.name: Bertie B
runners_data.note: Prominent style but 411-day absence and poor recent form makes him hard to fancy despite suitable running style
runners_data.spotlight: Has two wins over hurdles but was below his best in his last three starts, in 2025, and is still higher than his last winning mark; returns from a 411-day absence and may need to come down in the weights.

runners_data.name: Trust House
runners_data.note: Front-runner with progressive spring form but faces stablemate Castle Ivers and strong pace pressure early
runners_data.comment: On hat-trick after justifying favouritism at Market Rasen & Ffos Las (combined rise 16lb).
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive in the spring when winning at Market Rasen and Ffos Las over around 2m; no disgrace in finishing runner-up to stablemate Castle Ivers at Perth (2m, good to soft) last time; Sean Bowen prefers Castle Ivers on this occasion but still a contender up in trip.

races.paceDynamic: Castle Ivers, Continuance, and Trust House will ensure a strong gallop from the off, with all three confirmed front-runners likely to dispute the early lead. This pace will stretch the field and create a searching test of stamina over 2m4f on good ground. The sustained gallop will expose any fitness concerns and favor horses with proven staying power who can handle a true test. This race shape strongly favors prominent racers and hold-up horses with stamina, while early leaders may pay for their exertions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Suits Stayers
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners maintain a relentless pace throughout
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop will find out the fitness doubts of long-absent runners and favor those with proven stamina reserves. Hold-up horses like Oakley and Theatre Tom can benefit from the collapse of pace-setters in the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Gets Away
scenarios.trigger: If Castle Ivers or Trust House can steal a march turning for home
scenarios.body: The winner breaks clear while rivals are still organizing their challenges behind the strong early pace. Castle Ivers' step up in trip or Trust House's proven class at this level could prove decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses and a prominent racer times their move perfectly
scenarios.body: Speed Davis or Oakley can position ideally behind the leaders before striking in the final furlong. Their tactical speed and recent form gives them the edge over hold-up horses in a tactical finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners go too fast and fade before the home turn
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the last flight, suiting horses with tactical pace over pure stamina. Fitness concerns become less relevant but class and recent sharpness prove crucial.

watchPoints.text: Castle Ivers and Trust House are stablemates who both want to lead which could compromise each other's chances
Theatre Tom returns after 520 days off and is likely to need the run despite his style suiting the pace scenario
Speed Davis carries a penalty from his April win which could prove significant in a competitive handicap
Three confirmed front-runners could set up the race for a closer or hold-up horse if they go too fast early
Oakley has won both hurdle races at similar conditions and holds solid recent form claims despite rising in class

races.name: CopyBet Overnight Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Ebony Warrior
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 29-day break with inconsistent handicap record despite dual hurdle wins
runners_data.comment: Dual novice winner on good; hasn't really advertised his staying credentials since.
runners_data.spotlight: Dual hurdle winner (2m-2m5f, good) but yet to win in handicap company and was out of sorts in a light campaign last season; shaped as though the run may have been needed on last month's reappearance but remains with something to prove on recent evidence despite a further ease in the weights.

runners_data.name: The Long Walk
runners_data.note: Prominent type whose best efforts came when racing handily, 61 days off but yard in poor form lately
runners_data.spotlight: Mixed form last season; peak efforts included third at Market Rasen (2m2f) on Boxing Day and second off this mark at Hereford in April latest; not guaranteed to back that up but he's in the mix if repeating that effort with cheekpieces now added.

runners_data.name: Pike Road
runners_data.note: Natural front runner with two wins at this exact distance, likely uncontested lead with 5lb claimer reducing experience
runners_data.comment: Thorough stayer who was unsuited down in trip latest and that could find him out again.
runners_data.spotlight: Dual 2m7f hurdle winner last year, latest success at Uttoxeter (soft) in November off 2lb lower; followed that with a solid effort in a Class 2 at Cheltenham; form has dipped since but recent return may have been needed and he's worth considering with that run behind him.

runners_data.name: Eaton Anne
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who needs strong pace to aim at, tongue-tie added after recent chase near-miss
runners_data.comment: Fair runs over fences on last two starts; had wind op since latest run; has a chance
runners_data.spotlight: Dual hurdle winner who went close to breaking his duck over fences off this mark at Hexham (3m, good to soft) last month, with a tongue-tie added to refitted cheekpieces following a second wind operation; merits serious consideration back over hurdles with the stable in good form.

runners_data.name: Fairlawn Skipper
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with promise but yet to win over hurdles despite consistent placed efforts
runners_data.spotlight: Bumper winner last year; yet to add to that in five hurdle starts but has shown ability, notably when third at Newcastle (2m7f, good) in October; below-par effort in November and well held on last month's reappearance at Perth (3m2f, good to soft); may come on from that but others appeal more.

runners_data.name: Balkardy
runners_data.note: Unpredictable hold-up type returning to hurdles after chase unseating, hard to trust despite ability
runners_data.spotlight: 7-39, with three wins over hurdles, but he's hard to predict and was badly out of sorts in the autumn; unseated early on last month's return and reverts to hurdles off his last winning mark, but it's difficult to know what to expect.

runners_data.name: Impecunious
runners_data.note: Prominent runner stepping up from 2m5f debut for new yard, showed improved form when winning for previous trainer
runners_data.comment: Two wins last year and he ran well for long way on recent stable debut; could be dangerous
runners_data.spotlight: Two wins for Chris Down last year, latest at Newton Abbot (3m2f, good) off 3lb lower; well-held fourth of seven on stable/seasonal debut at Worcester (2m5f) but ran well for a long way; worth considering with that run behind him.

runners_data.name: Prince De Juilley
runners_data.note: Prominent type returning after 215-day break but had found form before absence with Stratford win
runners_data.spotlight: Came back to form in the autumn and gained a deserved success at Stratford (2m6f) in October, following that with two solid placed efforts off higher marks, latest at Hereford (3m2f) in November off 2lb lower and all on good ground; has a career-high mark to defy but is reliable and has gone well off a similar break before.

runners_data.name: Gwash
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose sole win came over two years ago, recent form suggests unlikely breakthrough
runners_data.comment: Best effort came when runner-up at Uttoxeter last July; well beaten in three runs since.
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to add to his sole win at Warwick (2m3f, good) over two years ago and recent evidence doesn't suggest a breakthrough is imminent; not dismissed completely but needs a revival.

runners_data.name: Peter's Last Deal
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse yet to build on promising debut third, long absence and poor recent effort concerning
runners_data.spotlight: Yet to build on November's promising hurdle debut when third at Hereford (2m3f, good), with progress interrupted by absences and he was always out the back when tailed off on his comeback run 28 days ago; probably capable of better in time but still best watched on handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Lacrima
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with French form hard to assess, blinkers and tongue-tie added after poor recent chasing efforts
runners_data.comment: Won four times in France but has been beaten 64l and 60l on his two starts in Britain.
runners_data.spotlight: Completed a hat-trick over fences in France last autumn, all around 2m2f on deep ground, but has shown little in three handicap chase runs for this stable this year; reverts to hurdles off a lower mark and the step up in trip needs to spark a turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Pike Road stands alone as the confirmed front runner and will likely dictate terms from the start, with The Long Walk, Ebony Warrior, Prince De Juilley and Impecunious tracking prominently behind. The lack of genuine pace pressure means Pike Road can steal a march and control the tempo, particularly dangerous given his two wins at this exact trip last year. With half the field comprising hold-up horses including Eaton Anne, Fairlawn Skipper, Balkardy and Lacrima, they'll need Pike Road to fold late to get competitive. This tactical scenario strongly favours the prominent runners who can position close enough to Pike Road to strike when the pace lifts.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pike Road Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Pike Road gets an uncontested lead and maintains his jumping rhythm
scenarios.body: The 7-year-old can dictate on his own terms like when winning twice at this trip last year, with no genuine pace rival to pressure him early. The hold-up brigade will have too much to do if he kicks approaching the final flight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle
scenarios.trigger: If The Long Walk or Prince De Juilley press Pike Road from the home turn
scenarios.body: This creates the ideal scenario for the prominent horses who can travel into contention without having to make ground from the rear. Both have shown their best form when able to race handily rather than from behind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Success
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely strong with multiple prominent horses going too fast
scenarios.body: Eaton Anne and Fairlawn Skipper would benefit most from a collapse ahead, having both shown their best form when staying on from off the pace. The smaller field works against this scenario developing.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Upset
scenarios.trigger: If the market principals underperform due to fitness or jumping errors
scenarios.body: Gwash has shown flashes of ability despite limited recent success, while Lacrima brings French form that's hard to assess. Both would need the pace to set up perfectly and the favourites to disappoint.

watchPoints.text: Pike Road's jumping rhythm early - any mistakes will invite pressure he's not used to handling
The Long Walk's position turning in - needs to be within striking distance to use his finishing kick effectively
Prince De Juilley's fitness after 215 days off - any signs of rustiness could derail his chances despite previous form
Eaton Anne's position at halfway - hold-up horses need Pike Road to go too fast to have any realistic chance
Weather changes affecting the going description - any softening would favour the French-bred Lacrima significantly
